key_insight: The paper introduces a parallel monolithic ALE finite-element solver that can simulate zero-mass-ratio vortex-induced vibrations of a flexible cylinder in 2D and 3D by coupling fluid forces, spring motion, and mesh deformation in one system.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable prediction of challenging fluid-structure interactions with massless structures, which is relevant for offshore, aerospace, and vibration-control applications where accurate VIV response matters.
method: Monolithic finite-element formulation in an arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework with implicit time stepping.
Mesh motion handled by a linear-elastic pseudo-solid model with variable Lamé coefficients.
No-slip enforced via a Lagrange multiplier coupled to cylinder position degrees of freedom, with distributed coupling strategies for parallel execution.
evidence_signal: The solver was verified with manufactured solutions, showed second-order time accuracy, reproduced prior 2D VIV results at Reynolds numbers 100–300, predicted nonperiodic 3D oscillations at Re = 300, and scaled to 768 compute cores with MUMPS.
watch_item: The approach relies on a direct solver (MUMPS), so memory and communication costs may limit practicality for much larger 3D problems.
paper_title: A parallel solver for vortex-induced vibrations at zero mass ratio
